user.title: Shopping list
user.description:
Language and country of the recipes. This decides the suggested recipe sites (e.g. Allrecipes for English, Marmiton for French), the language of dish names and shopping items, and the Cookidoo country. The interface language follows your Home Assistant profile.

Where should ingredients go? An existing to-do list (e.g. Bring!) or the planner's own list. Items follow the Bring! pattern: article as item, amount and dish in the description.

data_description.shopping_list: “Own list” creates “Essensplaner Einkaufsliste”, handy for testing.
data_description.region: German is tested live. The other languages use supported recipe sites whose search is not yet field-tested; a search agent with web search helps most there.

devices.title: Kitchen appliances
devices.description: Which devices do you own? Only dishes you can cook are proposed. Thermomix recipes need the Thermomix selected.

data_description.custom_devices: More devices, comma separated, e.g. “slow cooker, grill”.

ai.title: AI
ai.description:
Choose which AI creates the weekly suggestions. The meal planner then checks every dish itself: link, time, kcal and your rules.

**Easiest way, free: Google Gemini**
1. Create an API key at aistudio.google.com.
2. Add the “Google Gemini” integration in Home Assistant and paste the key.
3. Here: **Who makes the suggestions?** = AI in Home Assistant, **Main AI** = “Google AI Task”, **Create a new search agent at** = Gemini. Done, Cookidoo recipes are found too.

**Other providers:** Claude (“Anthropic” integration) and ChatGPT (“OpenAI Conversation”) work the same way but need credit with the provider. Never share API keys.

**External AI, for advanced users:** Instead of an AI in Home Assistant, a scheduled task in your Claude or ChatGPT subscription delivers the suggestions. You need an MCP connection to Home Assistant and remote access. Instructions appear in the card under Settings once selected.

data_description.proposals_from: Usually: AI in Home Assistant. External AI only if a scheduled task in an AI subscription delivers; if nothing arrives within 5 hours after the planning time, the main AI steps in.
data_description.ai_search: An agent with web search finds real recipe links, also on Cookidoo. Agents with web search switched on are marked “web search on”. “None”: the main AI only names dishes and the meal planner searches the recipe sites itself (not Cookidoo).
data_description.create_search_agent: Creates the agent “Essensplaner Rezeptsuche” with web search at the chosen provider and selects it above. Model per provider: Gemini gemini-3.8-flash (searched on the free tier in our test), Claude claude-haiku-5-5, ChatGPT gpt-6.1-terra; you can change it in the agent at any time. Your other agents and voice control stay unchanged. “No” = create nothing.
data_description.ai_task: Suggests the dishes and judges “low cholesterol”. Usually called “… AI Task”, e.g. “Google AI Task”.
data_description.ai_shopping_names: “1 red pepper, diced” becomes “Pepper”. Good for Bring!, which knows fixed items.

init.title: Essensplaner
init.description:
Configure how the meal planner works. Tap a section, change values and save. In short:
**Language and region** – country of recipes, recipe sites and language of proposals.
**Schedule** – when proposals arrive and when the choice closes.
**Shopping trips** – how often you shop and when ingredients go on the list.
**Calendar** – events that affect meals (e.g. guests).
**Rules and taste** – servings, cooking time, calories, preferences.
**Eating habits** – fixed rules like “soup at most once a week”.
**Diet** – proposals per week and how many e.g. vegetarian.
**Shopping list** – where ingredients go and what never goes on it.
**Recipe sources** – which sites are searched.
**Kitchen devices** – what you own (e.g. Thermomix) and how often to use it.
**AI** – which AI plans and searches.
**Display** – where the planner appears.

data_description.staples: Things you always have never go on the list. Comma separated; compounds are recognised (salt → sea salt).
data_description.skip_spices: On: dried spices are left out.
data_description.catalog: One per line, “recipe name = list name”, e.g. “passata = canned tomatoes”.

sources.title: Recipe sources
sources.description: Which sites are searched. Only enabled sites are used; every recipe is fetched and checked before it is proposed. Cookidoo, Rezeptwelt and Zaubertopf are Thermomix sites. Own sites: {custom}. {thermomix_note} {error}

data_description.new_source_url: Add a site: paste a link to any recipe of it. The integration tests reading it, then enables the site.

diet_count.title: Proposals per week
diet_count.description: How many dishes should be proposed per week? You don't have to take all. Next you set how many of them e.g. vegetarian.

data_description.recipes_per_week: Proposals per week, e.g. 10 for 7 days with some choice.

diet.title: Diet
diet.description: Per diet: **Off** = don't care, **Always** = every dish, **Count** = this many of the {recipes} dishes. A dish may count several times (vegan counts as vegetarian). Ingredients decide vegetarian/vegan/lactose-/gluten-free; low cholesterol is rated by the AI. Calories are under “Rules and taste”. {clamped}

data_description.vegetarian_count: Only for “Count”: at least this many per week.
data_description.vegan_count: Only for “Count”: at least this many per week.
data_description.lactose_free_count: Only for “Count”: at least this many per week.
data_description.gluten_free_count: Only for “Count”: at least this many per week.
data_description.low_cholesterol_count: Only for “Count”: at least this many per week.

diet_overlap.title: Note: overlaps required
diet_overlap.description: These counts only fit if at least {overlap} of {recipes} dishes meet several options at once. Save anyway?

device_counts.title: Appliances per week (optional)
device_counts.description: Optional: how many of the {recipes} dishes should use a device? 0 = don't care. Example: Thermomix 2 → at least two Thermomix dishes per week.

data.count_stove_oven: Stove and oven: dishes per week

data_description.count_stove_oven: At least this many dishes per week with this device. 0 = don't care.
data_description.count_thermomix: At least this many dishes per week with this device. 0 = don't care.
data_description.count_airfryer: At least this many dishes per week with this device. 0 = don't care.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.description: Once a week the planner proposes dishes for the coming week. Until the choice closes you pick what to cook; then unpicked dishes drop and the new week starts. Example: proposals Friday 18:00, choice closes Saturday 12:00.

data.dashboard_path: Dashboard path opened from the push (e.g. /essensplaner)

data_description.plan_weekday: On this day the AI creates next week's proposals automatically.
data_description.plan_time: Time of the automatic proposals. The search takes a few minutes, then the push follows.
data_description.deadline_weekday: Pick dishes until this day. The new meal week starts here.
data_description.deadline_time: Time the choice closes. Afterwards only picked dishes remain.
data_description.notify: Who gets a push for new proposals, released shopping or errors? Empty = no push.
data_description.dashboard_path: Page opened from the push, e.g. /essensplaner. Empty = the push just opens the app.

rules.title: Rules and taste
rules.description: Basic rules for every proposed dish. Hard limits (time, kcal) are checked by the integration on the real recipe, soft ones like taste by the AI. Based on {recipes} proposals per week.

data_description.kcal_aware: On: set kcal limits per serving in the next step. Off: calories don't matter.
data_description.portions: Servings to shop for; list amounts are scaled to it.
data_description.time_max: No dish takes longer than this total time per recipe.
data_description.time_quick: Up to this time a dish counts as “quick”.
data_description.quick_share: At least this many quick dishes per week.
data_description.profile: Free text for the AI: likes and dislikes, e.g. “Mediterranean, no offal, kids don't like spicy”.
data_description.max_same_main: E.g. 3: no more than three dishes with chicken, beef, pork, mince or salmon per week (detected from the dish name, wishes don't count). 0 = don't care.

trips.title: Shopping trips
trips.description: How often do you shop for the dishes per week? Each dish is assigned to a trip and its ingredients go on the list accordingly. Example with 2 trips: Saturday for Sat–Tue, Tuesday for Wed–Fri.
